# Survival gear visual review

Local Blender authored, stylized low-poly static props. No model-generation API was called. No animation, character rigging, economy, survival behavior, or garment fitting is implemented. Wearable assets are unoccupied gear forms, not characters. Geometry is authored in metres; every GLB is reimported and bounding dimensions compared with a 2 mm tolerance before rendering.

## Batch 01 — passed 10/10
Inspected actual 600 px Blender renders in output/batch01-review.png. All ten silhouettes fit within frame and have identifiable separate functions: backpack pockets and clasps, open plate carrier and shoulder bridges, helmet, dual-filter mask, belt, paired shin guards, boots, gloves, headlamp, and open-neck poncho. No bodies or characters are present. Material separation, dimensions, paired symmetry where appropriate, and intact exported components are visible. These are stylized bases: clothing is not a fitted or deformable garment simulation. No targeted repair or regeneration was performed.

## Batch 02 — passed 10/10
Inspected actual renders in output/batch02-review.png. Pry bar, hammer, hatchet, spade, cutters, serrated saw, wound spool, tool roll, crank radio and lantern have distinct silhouettes and complete visible parts. Thin tools remain legible against the background; saw teeth and spool winding resolve clearly. No clipping or missing materials observed. Tools are simplified static bases; cutting edges, cutter linkage and folding mechanisms are not functional or animated. All ten reimport scale checks passed. No regeneration or targeted repair.

## Batch 03 — passed 10/10 after three independent regenerations
First inspection rejected ZG022, ZG025 and ZG030 for excessive visual similarity to ZG021. Each entire base was independently regenerated once; no targeted repair. Reinspected output/batch03-review.png: a round tin with gauze rolls, open vial organizer and wheeled supply trunk now have clearly distinct shapes and parts. Other assets show filter pump, nested canteen, folded stretcher, blanket roll, splints and wash station. All previews are intact and within frame. All ten final GLB reimports pass metre-scale validation.

## Batch 04 — passed 10/10 after one independent regeneration
First review rejected the rolled ZG033 because its silhouette duplicated the emergency blanket roll. Independently regenerated the entire base once as an unrolled sleeping bag with pillow, quilting and zipper rail. Reinspected output/batch04-review.png: all ten now have distinct camp roles and shapes. The A-frame shelter has visible entry, stove burners and fuel bottle resolve, solar panel and battery are visible, tripod and suspended pot are intact, crossed chair legs read clearly, collector geometry drains toward center, and workbench has lower shelf and vice. Corrected the shelter's display label from 'Dome' to 'A-frame' to match actual geometry. Final GLB scale checks passed; no targeted repair.

## Batch 05 — passed 10/10
Inspected actual renders in output/batch05-review.png. Larger assets have distinct footprints and readable function: staggered L sandbag cover, timber barricade, fine-grid fence, striped gate, watch platform with ladder/rails, roadblock, elevated water tank, loaded rack, open-front booth, wheeled generator cart. All are contained in frame, with intact supports and contrasting components. Every GLB scale check passes. No regeneration or targeted repair.

## Final counts
50 distinct accepted bases; 50 GLBs and 50 asset PNG previews. Five reviewed batches of ten. 54 complete generation attempts: 46 accepted first attempts and four accepted independent second attempts. Four initial visual rejections, zero skipped IDs, zero targeted repairs. No claim of animation, functional machinery, medical effectiveness, structural certification or survival simulation. Production delivery is owned by the root app/release agent.
